shortName: University of Louisville School of Medicine
additionalCoursework:
Premedical students should develop a solid background in the humanities, psychology, sociology, philosophy, and the arts. Understanding human relationships and human nature is vital to the practice of medicine. Students are encouraged to take courses that would be difficult to acquire after the college experience is completed. The School of Medicine seeks to admit well-rounded students with broad and diverse educational experiences. 

Applicants must receive a letter grade of C or higher for all required prerequisite courses. Substitutions for the premedical science requirements can only be allowed if replaced by advanced work in the same area. Applicants will receive credit for any Spring 2020 pre-requisite course for which they receive a “pass” under a pass/fail grading system.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The HSC Office of Health Equity and Engagement at the University of Louisville welcomes and embraces our community of students, residents, fellows, faculty, and staff. We seek to encourage and foster the growth and development of all our constituents to help everyone succeed on our campus. By augmenting a culture and climate that demonstrates its belief that all add value to intellectual development, academic enrichment, patient care, research, and community engagement, we believe our campus will be at the forefront of opportunity and innovation.
Our vision is to be a national model in promoting health equity and inclusive innovation through excellence in education, research, patient care, and service.
Our mission is to create an inclusive environment that supports students and employees through evidence-based resources, advocacy, and support in learning, discovery, connection, and collaboration.
https://louisville.edu/access/centers-departments/office-health-equity-engagement
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students may petition in writing for a leave of absence of one year or less. A subcommittee of the Student Promotions Committee considers such requests, then submits its recommendation to the Dean for a final decision. Students requesting a leave should expect to appear before the subcommittee to discuss the reasons for the request. Students in good academic standing may obtain maternity or paternity leaves of absence for up to six months by appropriately submitting a written request. Extension of any leave of absence beyond the period originally granted requires a written petition and a personal appearance before the subcommittee to discuss the need for the extension.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The Office of Medical Student Affairs offers a variety of opportunities for student involvement. More information about available ULSOM Clubs and Organizations may be found at:  https://medicine.louisville.edu/learner-experience/medical-student-affairs
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The U of L SOM is located in the heart of downtown Louisville's bustling medical center, on the Health Sciences campus of the University of Louisville.  The city of Louisville, home to the Kentucky Derby, is a progressive community of 1.2 million people with a robust economy, a vibrant arts and entertainment scene, and a rich history infused with Southern hospitality.  Louisville has a bustling food and hospitality array as the "epicenter for New Southern Cuisine" and routinely ranks in the Top 10 Most Affordable Cities in America by Forbes. Explore more at https://louisville.edu/visits/living-louisville
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Students choose to live in apartments and houses in many neighborhoods throughout the greater Louisville area. Resources for non-University housing options are generated each year by current students and distributed to the incoming class through various channels, including email, panel discussions, and messaging threads. Additional available off-campus listings may be browsed at: https://offcampushousing.louisville.edu/listing
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: All students have access to support services through our Office of Medical Student Affairs.  https://medicine.louisville.edu/learner-experience/medical-student-affairs
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Medical Student Affairs Office Learning Team is dedicated to helping every medical student at the University of Louisville School of Medicine achieve academic excellence by developing learning skills, offering holistic support, and cultivating self-empowerment. https://medicine.louisville.edu/learner-experience/medical-student-affairs and https://louisville.edu/accessibility
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Recognizing the growing awareness of high levels of burnout among medical students, residents, and practicing physicians nationwide, the Dean's Office at ULSOM has implemented a "Being Well" initiative, including resources and programs to promote health, resilience, and compassion. These resources are designed to support the physical and emotional needs of the ULSOM community students, staff, and faculty and are in addition to the wellness programming offered through the ULSOM Office of Student Affairs. These offices also partner with initiatives across the University and Health Science campus that connect students with additional program offerings.

Each student is assigned a faculty Advisory Dean who meets with them at least 2 times per semester and provides emotional and academic support and career counseling. Each student is part of an Advisory College, which also provides peer leaders, college captains, and more senior students who can offer support.

Mental health counseling is readily available on the School of Medicine campus.

Academic support is available from learning specialists.

Lunch and Learns are offered on topics such as Introduction to Mindfulness, the Relationships in Medicine Panel, Sleep Science, etc.

Social events for students, including self-defense classes, cooking demonstrations, cornhole tournaments, trivia night, etc.

Service opportunities include the American Heart Association Walk, Thanksgiving Canned Food Drive, Unified Sports, American Red Cross Blood Drives, etc.

medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: The U of L SOM is committed to training humanistic and patient-centered physicians to meet Kentucky's diverse health care needs. The integrated curriculum is focused on providing comprehensive exposure to the fundamental aspects of medicine while retaining sufficient flexibility for effective development of each student's individual abilities, interests and specific visions. Four goals drive the design, development, implementation and evaluation of our curriculum: integration of basic and clinical sciences, within and across courses and clinical rotations; expanded use of non-lecture teaching and learning modalities, such as self-directed learning, small-group activities, and team-based learning; expanded use of technology to support teaching and learning, such as the learning and curriculum management systems, exam and evaluation software and patient simulations; and development of course and clerkship learning objectives that support the overall goals and educational objectives.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: All students must complete four weeks of clinical training at a site designated as underserved during the required third year family medicine clerkship.  The family medicine clerkship affords students an opportunity to work one-on-one with family physicians, experience the breadth and continuity of family medicine, and complete a service learning project which allows a more profound interaction with the community.  Third year students also complete six week pediatrics and eight week internal medicine rotations.  Fourth year students complete an acting internship (which can be in family medicine, internal medicine or pediatrics) and also complete ambulatory and intensive care rotations and a palliative care experience.  A subset of interested students in each class are admitted with the agreement that they will complete their third and fourth years in Madisonville, KY, a rural setting with a successful record of graduating students choosing primary care and rural service careers.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students have the opportunity to pursue research in a formal mentored summer research program between the first and second years of medical training. Students select from faculty project abstracts and are matched to laboratories in their area of interest.  In addition, medical students may apply for fellowships from the NIH and other public/private foundations.  A Distinction in Research track is available for selected students seeking a longitudinal research experience without lengthening medical school training; a faculty mentor guides them over three years in gaining clinical research skills and completing a research project. https://medicine.louisville.edu/learner-experience/md-learner-experience/md-program-distinction-tracks

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: The School of Medicine was established at the Louisville Medical Institute in 1833 and became affiliated with the University of Louisville in 1846. In 1970 the university became a member of the Kentucky state system of higher education.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
School of Medicine Mission Statement
Improve the health and vitality of our community, our commonwealth, and our world by educating the next generation of physicians and scientists, providing high-quality compassionate care, pursuing transformative research, forging strategic partnerships, and striving for inclusive excellence.

School of Medicine Vision Statement
Demonstrate and be recognized for excellence and leadership in education, research, clinical care, innovative partnerships, and diversity, equity & inclusion.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Two weeks; reduced time allowed in later stages of cycle according to AMCAS traffic rules. https://medicine.louisville.edu/admission/md-program-admissions
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
Each applicant is required to submit a pre-med advisory committee report. If your college/university does not have a pre-med committee, we require three (3) letters of recommendation. These letters must be on college letterhead and should include at least one letter from a faculty member who taught the applicant in an area of biology, chemistry, physics, or mathematics (BCPM); one letter from a faculty member in a course of the applicant’s choosing; and one professional letter, which may include a third academic letter, supervisor or a physician whom you shadowed. 

Applicant’s who have not been continuously enrolled for more than three (3) years may substitute one academic letter for a second professional letter if desired, but must have at least one faculty/academic reference. If you have been enrolled in a post baccalaureate or graduate program for one year at the time of application, one of your letters should come from a faculty member at your current institution.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Two one-on-one academically blinded interviews with members of our Admissions Committee.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Non-residents who have significant academic, personal, or family ties to Kentucky may be considered.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Considered in same manner as international applicants. For more information: https://medicine.louisville.edu/admission/md-program-admissions
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Most recent score is primary consideration, with prior scores also reviewed during full Admission Committee discussions, if applicant has been interviewed.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: We use national and school-generated MCAT and GPA historical data to screen for a high likelihood of medical school success. This includes but is not limited to the percentage of students with specific MCAT/GPA results passing Step 1 on their first attempt. Applicants with an MCAT below 498 are unlikely to receive ongoing consideration.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: We use national and school-generated MCAT and GPA historical data to screen for a high likelihood of medical school success; this includes but is not limited to the percentage of students with specific MCAT/GPA results passing Step 1 on their first attempt. Trends in GPA (total and BCPM) during undergraduate/graduate work are also reviewed. Applicants with a GPA  below 3.0 are unlikely to receive ongoing consideration.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: The classes taken, class specific grades and grade trends are considered.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Credit granted by junior/community colleges is accepted. All coursework must be graded to fulfill prerequisite requirements or be supplemented by graded, advanced work in the same subject area.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: We will accept letters of intent, but they are not considered a part of our admissions process. Letters of intent may be uploaded to the secondary application portal. Also, updates are not accepted unless we specifically request an academic update from an applicant.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Scholarships are limited and awarded based on merit, mission, and professional promise. Demonstrated financial need may be considered. The Scholarship Committee reviews AMCAS and secondary application materials to select scholarship recipients. The Office of Medical Student Financial Aid provides counseling and assists students in applying for aid. You may also review a listing of outside scholarships available through the Medical Student Financial Aid website, https://medicine.louisville.edu/learner-experience/md-scholarships-funding
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition is established by the Kentucky Council on Postsecondary Education with input from the University.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
In selecting courses, the student should be aware of the broad scope of the medical profession. The biological basis for the practice of medicine is traditional and appropriate because medicine, in its technical aspects, is an applied biological science. Modern medical practice also requires a working knowledge of chemistry and physics to appreciate vital processes in both health and disease. Successful medical students must be able to read rapidly and with understanding and express thoughts clearly and concisely.

The School of Medicine seeks to admit well-rounded students with broad and diverse experiences. Students should develop a solid background in the humanities, philosophy, and the arts. Understanding human relationships and human nature is vital to the practice of medicine. Students are encouraged to take courses that would be difficult to acquire after the college experience is completed.
medSchoolSelection.medSchoolMediaSites: Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, iTunesU, all accessible through School of Medicine Admissions webpage http://louisville.edu/medicine/admissions
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: If prerequisite coursework is older than 10 years old, the coursework should be supplemented by completion of recent science courses.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The U of L SOM is a state-supported institution that gives preference to Kentucky residents. Consistent with our mission as a state university, those with significant academic, personal, or family ties to Kentucky are given preference. Applicants are selected on the basis of their individual merits without bias concerning sex, race, creed, national origin, age, or handicap. Applicants are selected based on intellect, integrity, maturity, and interpersonal sensitivity. Consideration is given to the past academic record, college pre-professional committee evaluations/faculty letters of recommendation, extracurricular activities, and personal interviews held at the medical school and the Trover Campus.  Early completion of the application process, rather than waiting until the various deadlines approach, increases an applicant's competitiveness.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing is a valuable part of a broad evaluation of the demands and rewards of medicine. It allows the student to experience both the art and science of medicine, to see depthful knowledge and skills applied, relationships formed and deepened, and the necessary teamwork of modern medicine in action. It exposes the student to the supportive successes of the healthcare system and the frustrating blockades that sometimes impede sensitive desired care. It allows the student to more wisely choose medicine as a lifelong calling.
